claims.text: CoCrFeMnNi can be used as a transition material between diffusion-mediated and dislocation-mediated creep mechanisms.
The suitability of CoCrFeMnNi as a transition material is caused by its combination of lattice distortion and interface coherency.
The initial material is a CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy-alloy multilayer with a coherent interface.
The proposed intervention applies a uniaxial stress of 500 MPa at 800°C.
The proposed creep test is conducted in vacuum with a stated stress rate of 10^-4 s^-1.
Lattice distortion and interface coherency are the structural mediators of the proposed creep response.
The operative creep mechanisms are thermally activated dislocation glide and diffusion-mediated creep.
A coherent-interface CoCrFeMnNi multilayer will have 30% greater creep resistance than an incoherent-interface CoCrFeMnNi baseline.
The predicted change in creep resistance is to be evaluated using the steady-state creep rate.
The proposed baseline is CoCrFeMnNi with an incoherent interface.
The proposed operating boundary is 400–600 MPa and 750–850°C.
The role of interface coherency in the creep behavior of HEA multilayers remains unclear.
The effect of interface coherency may depend on alloy composition and microstructure.
The hypothesis is falsified if creep resistance increases by less than 20% relative to the incoherent-interface baseline.
